senses.gloss: m. (לָקַט; v. לֶקֶט) grain-gleaner, a sort of huckster dealing in grains bought up in small quantities.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 72b:14">B. Mets. 72ᵇ</cite> <he>מ״ש לוקט … יזיף מלקוט חבריה</he> ed. (Ms. M. throughout <he>לוקט</he>; Ms. R. a. ed. Ven. <cite ref="L00666"><he>לקוט</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 7) why is it different with the gleaner? Because, if he has none, he will borrow from a fellow-gleaner.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 72b:13">Ib.</cite> <he>עד שיצא השער ללו׳ ולמוכר</he> until the market price has been announced for (the goods of) the gatherer and the merchant alike; <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 6:1">Tosef. ib. VI, 1</cite> <he>ללוקח</he> (corr. acc.).—[<cite ref="Ketubot 54a">Keth. 54ᵃ</cite> <he>בלקוט</he> Ar., v. <cite ref="L00687"><he>לָקִיט</he></cite>.]—Pl. <he>לָקוֹטוֹת</he>. B. Mets. l. c. <he>היו של ל׳ … ושל כל אדם וכ׳</he> Ms. H. a. R. (v. Rabb. D. S. l. c.) if the gleaners’ goods (mixed goods) were worth four S’ah (and more) a Sela, and those of other people three &c.; [ed. <he>היו לְקוּטוֹת … ולכל אדם וכ׳</he> if the gleaned grains were worth &c.; Tosef. l. c. <he>היו לקוטות הולכות מארבע</he> (not <he>והולכות</he>).
